mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over a three-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.02 mean) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3% for three months, or the rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.03 mean) during episodes of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 4% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0% in one month compared to previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.01 mean) when UNRATE exceeds 4% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.015 mean) during three-month INDPRO < 98 episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month average AND CPIAUCSL > 12-month average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.02 mean) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.015 mean) during four-month HOUST > 12-month MA episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data reclassification event rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically coincides with short-term S&P 500 volatility and negative 5-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month AND UNRATE increases month-over-month in the same month
regime_hint: data reclassification or statistical artifact regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.02 mean) when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in Real Personal Income (implied by RSAFS and PAYEMS) below -2% for six consecutive months signals a protracted weakening in household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/PAYEMS-derived real income < -2% YoY for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.03 mean) during six-month episodes of real income < -2% YoY.
